reason: Not a new or correctly framed hypothesis. (1) DUPLICATE: a sparse-label detector fine-tune (ignore unlabelled voxels / nnPU) is already IDEAS I-113 (B7), deferred-after-deadline since 2026-09-06 (CONTEXT.md l.140, l.216, l.489). Attaching it to I-261 misfiles it, because I-261 is axial z-localisation just outside the 7 um match, a different mechanism. (2) MECHANISM MISMATCH in its own evidence (scratchpad r11_detect_out.json, 6bba): 431/595 = 72% of missing GT nodes are at or above the intensity threshold (10th percentile of matched GT), against 87% for matched GT. So they are mostly NOT dim. They are peakless in bright tissue: 31% have a raw local max within 5 um, against 70% of matched GT. That points to crowding and merged maxima, i.e. separability or resolution. An nnPU or ignore-unlabelled loss fixes unlabelled positives being trained as negatives, not merged peaks, so the claimed link from the facts to this candidate is unsupported. (3) VALUE: zero for this competition. R9 bars it before 29 Sep, head retrain is closed (CONTEXT.md l.1488, kill test FAIL), and the pool is 6bba-specific (44b6 has 7 of the 668 misses) while private is other embryos. The pool also caps at only +0.029 lab, and the lab is known to over-trust these numbers (edge filter +0.016 lab, 0 on LB). (4) FEASIBILITY is trivial: it does nothing to #37/#38, is byte-identical and breaks no rule. However, the evidence path is in a temporary session scratchpad, not the repo, so the numbers must be copied, not linked.
